title: Use patterns, doubling and halving to work out other multiplication facts

lesson.title: Double It! Turning 2 Times Facts into 4 Times Facts

steps.say: You already know your two times facts really well, like two times seven is fourteen. Today we will use a little trick called doubling to turn those two times facts into four times facts, so you never have to guess.

Here is why doubling works. Four rows of seven is just two rows of seven, and then two more rows of seven. The blue part on top is the two times fact you already know, and the whole picture is twice as much.

visual.caption: Four rows of seven. The shaded top part is two rows of seven.

steps.say: Let's try it. Imagine four packs of maple cookies with seven cookies in each pack. Start with what you know: two times seven is fourteen. Now double fourteen. Fourteen and fourteen more is twenty eight. So four times seven is twenty eight cookies.

visual.caption: Start at 14, double it, and land on 28.

steps.say: Let's check on the hundred chart by hopping in sevens: seven, fourteen, twenty one, twenty eight. Four hops of seven lands right on twenty eight, exactly where doubling took us. Our trick works.

Careful with one common slip. Some children double the seven as well and say four times fourteen is fifty six. That is too big! We double the answer, not the size of each pack. Count the dots: four groups of seven really is twenty eight.

visual.caption: Four groups of seven dots — twenty eight in all.

steps.say: And the trick works backwards too. If you know four times seven is twenty eight, then halving twenty eight gives fourteen, which is two times seven. Doubling and halving are best friends.

lesson.answer: To find a four times fact, take the two times fact you know and double the answer — not the number in each group.

practice.question: At a Kelowna fruit stand, one small basket of blueberries costs nine dollars. You already know two baskets cost eighteen dollars. Picture a hundred chart in your head: start at eighteen and double it to find the cost of four baskets. How much is that?
practice.answer: Thirty six dollars. Double eighteen is thirty six, because four times nine equals thirty six.
